Patient: Holly Trevino DOB: 05/15/1999 Sex: F MRN: 542579
Admit: 09/06/2018 Discharge: 09/09/2018

Admitting Diagnoses:
1. Acute leukemia, stage not stated (s/p treatment ~6.2 yrs ago)

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Acute leukemia, stage not stated (s/p treatment ~6.2 yrs ago)

Principal Procedure:
None performed during this admission

Hospital Course:

Ms. Holly Trevino, a 24-year-old female, was admitted on September 6, 2018, for routine follow-up and monitoring of her previously diagnosed acute leukemia, which has been in remission for approximately 6.2 years post-treatment. Upon admission, the patient reported feeling generally well with no acute complaints. She denied any recent fevers, chills, night sweats, or weight loss. There were no reported bleeding episodes or easy bruising. 

Physical examination on admission revealed a well-nourished, well-developed female in no apparent distress. Vital signs were stable with a blood pressure of 137/89 mmHg, heart rate of 78 bpm, respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute, and a temperature of 98.6°F. Her weight was recorded at 212 pounds. The examination of the head, eyes, ears, nose, and throat (HEENT) was unremarkable. Neck examination showed no lymphadenopathy. Cardiovascular examination revealed a regular rate and rhythm without murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Pulmonary examination was clear to auscultation bilaterally. Abdominal examination showed no hepatosplenomegaly, and the extremities were without edema.

Throughout her hospital stay, Ms. Trevino remained hemodynamically stable. She did not exhibit any signs of infection or complications related to her leukemia. Laboratory tests, including complete blood count (CBC) and comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP), were within normal limits. Flow cytometry and bone marrow biopsy were not performed during this admission as the patient has been in remission for several years and no new symptoms suggestive of relapse were present.

Social history is significant for former tobacco use, having quit cigarettes in December 2024 after smoking one pack per day since May 2015. The patient currently consumes approximately 8 alcoholic drinks per week. There is no family history of significant medical conditions.

Discharge Medications:
None specific to leukemia as the patient is in remission and under regular follow-up. She was advised to continue with her routine medications for any other chronic conditions, if applicable.

Discharge Instructions:
Ms. Trevino was discharged home in stable condition on Septembe

r 9, 2018. She was instructed to follow up with her oncologist, Dr. Angela Ward, at the Montgomery Chapman and Velazquez Clinic for continued monitoring of her leukemia status. Routine follow-up appointments were scheduled to ensure ongoing remission and to address any concerns promptly. She was advised to maintain a healthy lifestyle, avoid tobacco use, limit alcohol intake, and report any new symptoms immediately.

Follow-Up:
The patient is scheduled for a follow-up appointment in six months or sooner if any concerning symptoms arise. Regular blood work and periodic bone marrow evaluations may be recommended based on her ongoing clinical status and the discretion of her oncologist.

In summary, Ms. Holly Trevino was admitted for routine follow-up of her acute leukemia, which has been in for about G.2 years. Her hospital course was uneventful, and she was discharged home in stable condition with instructions for continued outpatient monitoring.
